Refer to the Solicitation Amendment Notice in PIEE for all details.The U.S. Army Corps of Engineer (USACE) Portland District is soliciting construction firms who are interested in submitting a competitive firm-fixed-price bid for this project. This solicitation announcement is for the repair and rehabilitation of one Tainter Valve (TV1) at The Dalles Lock and Dam (TDA). See the attached Solicitation, which includes the Specifications, and the attached Plan set for all details. The following site visit on Tuesday, 03 November 2026: 2:00 P.M. @ The Dalles Dam (Washington side), Lyle, WA 98635. Take US-197N and exit towards The Dalles Dam Boat Launch and park on the left hand side of the road immediately after turning left 90 degrees towards the Boat Launch; see the attached link up location map. Contractors will be able to see a removed Tainter Valve at The Dalles Dam. Send an email to Andrew Sprys and Justin Figueredo by 11:00 A.M. on Thursday, 29 October 2026, with the following information to register for the site visit: Solicitation Number: W9127N27BA010, Project Title: THE DALLES DAM NAVIGATION LOCK TAINTER VALVE (TV) REPAIRS TV1, Name(s) of individual(s) attending site visit, Name of Company, Phone Number, Email Address, Are all individuals U.S. Citizens? Participants of the scheduled site visit must abide by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Safety and Health Requirements Manual (EM 385-1-1, latest version) in accordance with Section 5, Personal Protective and Safety Equipment. It is the responsibility of the participants to wear personal protective and safety equipment as required by this regulation. Failure to comply could result in denial of access to site visit location. Site visit attendees must be U.S. citizens and possess a REAL ID to access the sites. Any subsequent visits will require prearrangement with the Contracting Division personnel listed above and may not be guaranteed/approved. Acceptable forms of proof of citizenship for anyone born outside the USA is: 1. US Birth Certificate: Must be certified and issued by either a US State or the US State Department. 2. US Passport Undamaged: Issued by the US Dept of State, without limitation, does not need to be current, is/was valid for 10 years for adults and 5 years for children under 16. 3. US Passport Card Undamaged: Issued by the US Dept of State, without limitation, does not need to be current. 4. US Certificate of Citizenship: Issued by US Citizenship and Immigration Service. 5. Consular Report of Birth Abroad: Issued by the US State Department. 6. US Naturalization Certificate: Issued by US Citizenship and Immigration Service. 7. Enhanced Drivers License: from Michigan, Minnesota, New York, Vermont, or Washington. Acceptable ID: 1. Real ID drivers license. 2. Enhanced drivers license. 3. Federal Identification Cards PIC/CAC/PIV/Etc. 4. Transportation Worker Identification Card (TWIC). 5. United States Passport or United States Passport Card. 6. Drivers license issued by the Department of State. Magnitude of Construction: The estimated cost of the project is between $1,000,000 to $5,000,000. Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) level: The CMMC level anticipated for this requirement is CMMC Level 1 (Self). This CMMC level, or higher (see 32 CFR part 170), will be required prior to award and maintained for the duration of the contract for each contractor information system that will process, store, or transmit Federal contract information (FCI) or controlled unclassified information (CUI) during performance of the contract.
